title: Fisheye
description: A fisheye in fisheye cinematography is a very wide curvilinear projection that bends straight lines, especially away from the center. The world wraps around the lens; architecture becomes a bowl rather than a rectilinear box.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Put a face in the middle and the room circles them. Put them off-center and their skull stretches along the barrel.
The mapping can be circular (a round image in a black frame) or diagonal (the circle fills the rectangle). Either way, the mind of the shot is warped, or the space is a dome.
It is the wrong tool when you wanted extreme width with straight walls. That is a rectilinear 14mm Ultra-Wide.
Random wobbly architecture is a model failure, not fisheye projection. If the beat is only a mildly wide room, 24mm Wide already does it without the wrap.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Choose circular or full-frame fisheye and stage faces near the center unless edge stretching is deliberate. Keep the distortion systematic: lines bow around a stable center, they do not ripple.
A zenith or dome shot will map the room as a globe. Prompt: Fisheye on [Subject], circular or extreme barrel distortion, a world wrapping around a face, subjective unreality.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it when the mind is warped, or the space is a dome: a palace that should feel wrong, a subjective spiral, a helmet-cam joke. Do not use it as a synonym for 14mm, and do not apply random warping.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: 14mm Ultra-Wide is rectilinear: huge field, straight-ish lines, stretch from a close stand. Fisheye is curvilinear by design.
24mm Wide is moderate and polite. Kaleidoscope multiplies fragments; fisheye is one continuous wrap.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: The Favourite bends palace interiors under conspicuously wide, curvilinear views. Poor Things uses highly distorted wide-angle views so the world stays unfamiliar.
A Clockwork Orange and Being John Malkovich have used extreme wide wrap as subjective pressure. Grammar of bowing space, not a filter preset.

sections.title: Prompt it

blocks.text: Name the projection. Fisheye on [Subject], circular or extreme barrel distortion, a world wrapping around a face, subjective unreality.
Say whether the image is a circle or fills the frame, and keep the face near center unless stretch is the point. Do not write 14mm rectilinear, and do not ask for random wobble.

A palace official stands small at the center of an enormous ornate chamber, filmed with a frame-filling fisheye look. Walls bow smoothly toward the edges, ceiling and floor remain structurally coherent. Slow restrained action, locked camera, no circular black border.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is 14mm Ultra-Wide with extra warp, or a wavy hallucination. The tell is straight walls that should bow, or unstable rippling.
Fix: systematic barrel around a clear center, horizon curved, face protected unless you mean the stretch.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is fisheye in film?
It is a curvilinear ultra-wide projection that bends straight lines away from the center. The field wraps around the lens instead of drawing a rectilinear box.
Fisheye vs 14mm Ultra-Wide
A 14mm rectilinear ultra-wide keeps lines mostly straight and exaggerates size from a close stand. A fisheye bows those lines on purpose. Width is not the same as wrap.
When should I use fisheye?
Use it when unreality, comedy, or a dome of space is the point. Skip it for ordinary wides and for rectilinear 14mm intrusion.
How do I prompt fisheye for AI image or video?

Write: Fisheye on [Subject], circular or extreme barrel distortion, a world wrapping around a face, subjective unreality. Specify circular versus full-frame fill. Forbid random wobble and rectilinear 14mm.
